models.title: Allowance for doubtful accounts as a fraction of gross receivables
models.summary: The owner reconstructs gross receivables by adding the allowance to net receivables, then divides the allowance by that gross amount.

relationship.locator: Management discussion and analysis, Accounts Receivable—Trade, printed pp40–41; ratio table on p41
relationship.translation_notes: Both inputs are same-date monetary balances; the output is dimensionless and equals the displayed percentage divided by 100.

variables.definition: Positive contra-asset balance deducted from gross receivables
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Reported receivables after the same allowance and before any other unmodeled offsets
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Allowance divided by reconstructed gross accounts receivable
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: Allowance is the nonnegative positive magnitude of the same contra-asset deduction from the net receivables figure.
The net amount does not contain additional offsets that would prevent gross reconstruction, and both inputs use the same reporting date, currency and entity.
limitations: A reported allowance is an estimate and need not equal realized credit losses.
If other valuation offsets are included in net receivables, add back the correct offsets separately before calculating the fraction.
